content.text:
<title>Sallowfield Dental Group: monthly operations meeting</title>
<transcript>
[0] Mirela Stanek: Morning, everyone.
[1] Mirela Stanek: This is the monthly operations meeting for Sallowfield Dental Group.
[2] Mirela Stanek: Is Tobias on the line?
[3] Tobias Ferrant: I'm here.
[4] Tobias Ferrant: Bad signal in the car park, so shout if I drop out.
[5] Mirela Stanek: Will do.
[6] Mirela Stanek: First item is the booking system.
[7] Mirela Stanek: Hana, where are we?
[8] Hana Olund: We switched all three clinics to the new booking system on the first of September.
[9] Hana Olund: That was Marsh Road, Kiln Street and Abbey Row.
[10] Mirela Stanek: And the reminders?
[11] Hana Olund: Text reminders go out two days before an appointment and again on the morning.
[12] Hana Olund: Patients can confirm or cancel by replying.
[13] Tobias Ferrant: What has that done to missed appointments?
[14] Hana Olund: Before the switch, 14 percent of appointments were missed across the group.
[15] Hana Olund: In October it was 9 percent.
[16] Tobias Ferrant: That's a real drop.
[17] Hana Olund: It is, but it is not even.
[18] Hana Olund: Marsh Road is down to 6 percent.
[19] Hana Olund: Abbey Row is still at 13.
[20] Mirela Stanek: Why is Abbey Row behind?
[21] Hana Olund: A lot of Abbey Row's patients are older and many of them gave us a landline number.
[22] Hana Olund: A landline cannot receive a text.
[23] Tobias Ferrant: So the system is fine and the phone numbers are the problem.
[24] Hana Olund: Mostly, yes.
[25] Hana Olund: We have mobile numbers for about half of Abbey Row's patients.
[26] Mirela Stanek: What do you want to do about it?
[27] Hana Olund: I want reception at Abbey Row to phone the landline patients the day before.
[28] Hana Olund: It is about 40 calls a day.
[29] Tobias Ferrant: I disagree with that.
[30] Tobias Ferrant: Forty calls a day is most of a receptionist's morning, and we are already short at Abbey Row.
[31] Hana Olund: It is less than it sounds.
[32] Hana Olund: Most of them are a one-minute call.
[33] Tobias Ferrant: I would rather ask for a mobile number when they next come in, and wait.
[34] Mirela Stanek: We can do both for a month and look at the numbers.
[35] Mirela Stanek: Hana, run the calls in November.
[36] Mirela Stanek: Tobias, get reception asking for mobile numbers.
[37] Tobias Ferrant: Fine.
[38] Tobias Ferrant: One month.
[39] Mirela Stanek: Cost.
[40] Mirela Stanek: What are we paying for the system?
[41] Hana Olund: It is 380 pounds a month per clinic.
[42] Tobias Ferrant: So 1,140 a month for the group.
[43] Hana Olund: Yes.
[44] Hana Olund: Sorry, I need to correct one thing I said earlier.
[45] Hana Olund: The October figure for missed appointments across the group was 10 percent, not 9.
[46] Hana Olund: I read the wrong column.
[47] Hana Olund: Nine percent was the first week of November.
[48] Mirela Stanek: So 14 percent before, 10 percent in October.
[49] Hana Olund: Yes.
[50] Hana Olund: The clinic figures I gave are right.
[51] Mirela Stanek: Does it pay for itself?
[52] Hana Olund: A missed appointment costs us about 55 pounds in lost chair time.
[53] Hana Olund: We have roughly 2,600 appointments a month across the group.
[54] Tobias Ferrant: I'm not going to do that sum in a car park.
[55] Mirela Stanek: Nobody is asking you to.
[56] Mirela Stanek: Hana, put the sum in the notes.
[57] Hana Olund: I will.
[58] Mirela Stanek: Anything that went wrong with the switch?
[59] Hana Olund: One thing.
[60] Hana Olund: For the first week the system sent reminders for appointments that had already been cancelled.
[61] Hana Olund: We had 23 complaints.
[62] Mirela Stanek: Is that fixed?
[63] Hana Olund: The supplier fixed it on the ninth of September.
[64] Hana Olund: We have had no complaints about it since.
[65] Tobias Ferrant: I had patients telling me, "I cancelled that last week, why are you texting me?"
[66] Tobias Ferrant: It was embarrassing.
[67] Mirela Stanek: Understood.
[68] Mirela Stanek: Last item, staffing.
[69] Mirela Stanek: Tobias?
[70] Tobias Ferrant: We have hired a second hygienist for Kiln Street.
[71] Tobias Ferrant: She starts on the twelfth of January.
[72] Mirela Stanek: Good.
[73] Mirela Stanek: And Abbey Row reception?
[74] Tobias Ferrant: Still one person short.
[75] Tobias Ferrant: I am interviewing two people next week.
[76] Mirela Stanek: Then we will look at Abbey Row again in December, with the November numbers.
[77] Mirela Stanek: Thank you, both.
[78] Hana Olund: Thanks, Mirela.
[79] Tobias Ferrant: Thanks.
[80] Tobias Ferrant: I'm going back inside.
</transcript>

points.text: All three clinics (Marsh Road, Kiln Street, Abbey Row) switched to the new booking system on 1 September.
Text reminders go out two days before an appointment and again on the morning; patients can confirm or cancel by replying.
Missed appointments across the group fell from 14 percent before the switch to 10 percent in October (corrected from 9 percent; 9 percent was the first week of November).
Marsh Road's missed-appointment rate is down to 6 percent, while Abbey Row is still at 13 percent.
Abbey Row lags because many older patients gave landline numbers that cannot receive texts; mobile numbers are held for only about half of its patients.
Hana proposed that Abbey Row reception phone landline patients the day before, about 40 calls a day; Tobias objected on staffing grounds and preferred collecting mobile numbers.
Decision: do both for one month. Hana runs the calls in November and Tobias has reception ask for mobile numbers; Abbey Row will be reviewed in December with the November numbers.
The system costs 380 pounds a month per clinic, 1,140 pounds a month for the group.
A missed appointment costs about 55 pounds in lost chair time, with roughly 2,600 appointments a month across the group; Hana will put the payback sum in the notes.
In the first week the system sent reminders for already-cancelled appointments, producing 23 complaints; the supplier fixed it on 9 September and there have been no complaints since.
A second hygienist has been hired for Kiln Street, starting 12 January.
Abbey Row reception is still one person short; Tobias is interviewing two candidates next week.
